title: Bold, italic, small and code
summary: strong, em, small and code each have a default look you can restyle with CSS.
explanation: strong (importance), em (emphasis), small (side comments) and code (code) are inline elements with meaning, and each comes with a browser default: bold, italic, smaller and monospace.
Those defaults are just CSS. Here strong is set to a semi-bold 600, code gets a monospace font, a tinted background and a slightly smaller size so it does not look too big beside the text.
Choose the element for its meaning, then style it. Do not use strong just to make something bold.
tryThis: Remove the font-size from .text code: monospace fonts look larger than the text around them.
Give .text em font-style: normal and a colour instead: emphasis without italics.
